paragraphs.source_en: As you can see, the concept of entropy provides a precise version of the "easy versus difficult" conclusion we found earlier. It's easy for the pages of War and Peace to fall out of order because there are so many out of-order arrangements. It's difficult for the pages to fall in perfect order because hundreds of pages would need to move in just the right way to land in the unique sequence Tolstoy intended. It's easy for an egg to splat ter because there are so many ways to splatter. It's difficult for an egg to unsplatter, because an enormous number of splattered constituents must move in perfect coordination to produce the single, unique result of a pristine egg resting on the counter. For things with many constituents, going from lower to higher entropy-from order to disorder- is easy, so it happens all the time.
